gaps.sentence: It was the first time ___ I had ever driven on my own.
gaps.hint: after 'the first time', use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'The first time that ...' is the standard pattern; the pronoun may also be omitted, but 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

gaps.sentence: The person to ___ I addressed the letter has moved house.
gaps.hint: after a preposition, the object form for people
gaps.explanation: After a preposition the object pronoun 'whom' is required for people; 'that' and 'who' cannot follow a preposition.

gaps.sentence: It is one of the most impressive buildings ___ I have ever seen.
gaps.explanation: After superlative expressions, 'that' is the standard relative pronoun in defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: The girl ___ sits behind me in class is from Peru.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to a person who is the subject; 'which' refers only to things.

gaps.sentence: The festival, during ___ the town is full of visitors, takes place in July.
gaps.hint: preposition + event in a non-defining clause
gaps.explanation: 'During which' is the formal pattern; 'during when' does not exist.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ produces these parts has factories in three countries.
gaps.explanation: A company takes 'which' as subject; 'who' is normally reserved for individual people.

gaps.sentence: I will always remember the summer ___ we cycled along the Danube.
gaps.explanation: 'When' relates to a time expression like 'the summer'.

gaps.sentence: She was two hours late, ___ annoyed the interviewer.
gaps.hint: comment on the whole situation before the comma
gaps.explanation: When a clause comments on the whole previous statement, use 'which' after the comma.
